## Submission 188: TensorWave Open Source Developer Program (up to $250K AMD GPU Credits)

- Category: Cloud Providers
- Source Link: https://go.tensorwave.com/open-source-developer-program
- Amount: Up to $250,000 in MI300X compute credits per developer (sized to the proposal; multiple proposals allowed)
- Difficulty: 4/5 (Hard)
- Expires At: N/A

### Description

TensorWave gives **up to $250,000 in free compute credits on AMD Instinct MI300X** GPUs to developers who add or improve AMD GPU support in open-source AI/ML projects (think kernels, frameworks, training/inference stacks, devtools). It is a **proposal-based grant**, not a self-serve free tier — you pitch a concrete OSS contribution and TensorWave decides how many credits to award based on scope, impact and feasibility.

TensorWave is a US neocloud whose entire bet is AMD-only, ROCm-native infrastructure (they raised $100M to build the world's largest liquid-cooled AMD GPU deployment and also run the *Beyond CUDA* podcast/summit). The OSS Developer Program is essentially their way of paying outside engineers to widen the moat: more PyTorch / vLLM / SGLang / Triton / inference-engine code that runs well on MI300X means more customers for TensorWave.

---

## Who this is for

Great fit:
- Maintainers / regular contributors to OSS AI/ML projects (PyTorch, JAX, vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, ggml, Triton, Unsloth, TRL, axolotl, ScalarLM, ComfyUI, diffusers, etc.) who want to ship MI300X support, perf fixes, ROCm-native kernels, or bug fixes.
- Researchers porting CUDA-only code paths to ROCm / HIP.
- Independent kernel authors writing AMD-targeted ops (HIP, Composable Kernel, AITER, Triton-on-ROCm).

Bad fit:
- Closed-source commercial products (this is **OSS-only**).
- "I want to fine-tune a model for my SaaS" — that's a normal paid workload, not an OSS contribution. Use TensorWave's commercial pricing or another grant.
- Pure inference of someone else's model with no upstream contribution. Without the contribution angle there is nothing to evaluate.

---

## What you actually get

- Compute credits redeemable on TensorWave's AMD Instinct MI300X infrastructure (cloud GPU instances; bare-metal nodes and managed Kubernetes are also possible depending on the proposal).
- **"Up to $250,000"** is the maximum — most awards will be a fraction of that, sized to the project. For context, TensorWave's public MI300X price is roughly **$1.50–$1.71 / GPU-hour**, so $250K ≈ 145,000+ MI300X GPU-hours, and a more typical $5K–$25K grant still buys thousands of GPU-hours.
- 1× MI300X has 192 GB HBM3 — enough VRAM to load a 405B-parameter model on a single 8-GPU node, so the credits go a *long* way for both training and inference work.
- Implicit access to the TensorWave / AMD ecosystem (engineers, ROCm builds, sometimes cross-promotion of your contribution).

Not included:
- No cash, no equity, no salary — only compute credits.
- No hardware shipped to you — everything runs in TensorWave's cloud.
- Credits are tied to the proposed project; expect them to be scoped to that work, not freely usable for unrelated experiments.

---

## Registration (Step-by-Step)

1. Have an open-source AI/ML project in mind that needs AMD/ROCm work — either one you already maintain or one where you have credibility (existing PRs, issues filed, etc.).
2. Go to the application page: [go.tensorwave.com/open-source-developer-program](https://go.tensorwave.com/open-source-developer-program).
3. Submit a proposal that covers, at minimum: the project, the specific AMD GPU work (kernels? backend port? perf fixes? new feature?), why it matters, an estimate of compute needed (GPU-hours × GPU type), a rough timeline, and proof of your track record (GitHub profile, links to merged PRs).
4. You can submit **1 or multiple proposals** — TensorWave explicitly allows batched submissions, so it's fine to pitch "vLLM MoE kernel + SGLang FP8 attention + Triton-ROCm fused softmax" as three separate asks.
5. Wait for TensorWave's team to evaluate. Reviewers care most about: (a) does this actually improve the AMD/ROCm OSS ecosystem, (b) is the contributor able to ship it, (c) is the requested compute reasonable.
6. If approved, you get a TensorWave account + credit grant scoped to the project. Spin up MI300X instances, do the work, ship the upstream PR.

**Important:**
- The page is sometimes flaky or returns 404 to non-browser fetches — open it in a real browser. If it stays down, the program is also routinely promoted by TensorWave's co-founder Jeff Tatarchuk on LinkedIn / X (@TensorWaveCloud); reach out there if the form is broken.
- No credit card is required to *apply*, but TensorWave will likely want to verify identity / GitHub before granting compute.
- Expect the team to negotiate scope down — if you ask for the full $250K with a one-line proposal, the realistic outcome is either a much smaller grant or a request for more detail.

---

## Hardware You Get Access To

| GPU | VRAM | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **AMD Instinct MI300X** | 192 GB HBM3 | Primary platform for the program. 8-GPU nodes are standard; a single node fits a 405B-parameter model. |
| AMD Instinct MI325X / MI355X | 256 GB / 288 GB HBM3E | TensorWave's newer SKUs; access depends on availability and proposal fit. |

ROCm is the supported software stack (PyTorch and Hugging Face run natively on ROCm 7+; `rocm-smi` and drivers are pre-loaded on TensorWave images). Bring HIP / Triton / Composable Kernel / AITER if you're writing low-level code.

---

## Good Proposal Ideas (for inspiration)

- Add or fix MI300X support in a popular OSS inference engine (vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, ExLlamaV2, MLC-LLM, etc.).
- Write performant ROCm kernels for ops that are currently CUDA-only or slow on AMD (FP8 attention, MoE routing, fused linear+activation, custom samplers).
- Port a CUDA-specific training trick (FlashAttention variant, sequence parallel, fp4) to ROCm/HIP.
- Add MI300X CI to an OSS project so regressions get caught upstream instead of in user reports.
- Benchmark + tune an OSS framework on MI300X and contribute the perf fixes back.
- Build / improve OSS evaluation harnesses on AMD hardware.

---

## Catches & Things to Watch

- **Ongoing program, no fixed deadline** — but credit awards are at TensorWave's discretion and almost certainly capped by an annual budget, so applying earlier in the year is probably better than later.
- **OSS license required.** Closed-source / source-available / non-commercial-only licenses likely don't qualify. If your project is OSI-approved (Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD, GPL, MPL), you're fine.
- **You actually have to ship.** If you take credits and never land the upstream PR, do not expect a second grant.
- **US-based provider.** Workloads run in TensorWave's US data centers — fine for almost everyone but worth knowing if you have data-residency constraints.
- **Not a substitute for a normal free tier.** If you just want a few hours to try MI300X without writing OSS code, this is the wrong program — try the AMD Developer Cloud instead (link below).
- The landing page has been observed to return 404 to bare HTTP requests (anti-bot / marketing-page behaviour). Use a real browser; if the form is genuinely down, ping TensorWave on LinkedIn / X.

---

## Alternatives if you don't qualify

- **AMD Developer Cloud** — AMD's own free MI300X access for developers, lower bar but smaller allocations: [amd.com/en/developer/resources/cloud-access/amd-developer-cloud.html](https://www.amd.com/en/developer/resources/cloud-access/amd-developer-cloud.html).
- **AMD Instinct GPU Eval via TensorWave** — official AMD-sponsored evaluation track for testing models/workflows on MI300X: [amd.com/en/products/accelerators/instinct/eval-request/tensorwave.html](https://www.amd.com/en/products/accelerators/instinct/eval-request/tensorwave.html).
- **Prime Intellect Fast Compute Grants** — $500–$100K credit grants for OSS / distributed AI work (hardware-agnostic, includes AMD via aggregated providers).
- **Lambda / Nebius / HOSTKEY research grants** — broader academic / OSS compute grant programs on NVIDIA hardware.

## Submission 187: Stripe Atlas - $2,500 Stripe credits + $50K+ partner perks (incl. AI credits)

- Category: Startup Programs

- Amount: $2,500 Stripe credits + $50,000+ partner perks (incl. ~$5K AWS, $500 Anthropic, up to $2,500 OpenAI, $10K DigitalOcean, 30-90% HubSpot, etc.)

### Description

Incorporate a Delaware **C-Corp or LLC via Stripe Atlas** for a **$500 one-time fee** and unlock **$2,500 in Stripe processing credits** plus **$50,000+ in partner perks** including **AWS ($5,000)**, **Anthropic ($500 Claude API + highest rate limits)**, **OpenAI (up to $2,500 in API credits)**, **HubSpot (30% off, or 90% off if VC/accelerator-backed)**, **Mercury**, **Carta**, **Google Cloud**, **DigitalOcean**, and many more. The perks are designed for newly-incorporated founders who need cloud, AI, banking, equity, and CRM tooling on day one.

**Bottom line for AI builders:** if you're already planning to incorporate a US C-Corp, $500 → $2.5K Stripe + ~$3K combined OpenAI/Anthropic credits + $5K AWS makes the math trivial. If you're not actually going to use Stripe or run a US entity, the headline "$50K+" number is mostly noise — most perks are *discounts*, not free credits.

---

## Registration (Step-by-Step)

1. Go to [stripe.com/atlas](https://stripe.com/atlas) and click **"Start your company"**
2. Sign in with a **Stripe account** (or create one)
3. Choose entity type: **Delaware C-Corporation** (default, recommended for VC-track) or **Delaware LLC**
4. Fill in: company name, founder details (passport for non-US founders), share structure (default: 10M authorized, 8M issued), founder equity split
5. **Pay the $500 one-time fee** by card. This covers: Delaware filing (with expedited next-day processing), EIN acquisition, founder stock issuance, 83(b) election filing, registered agent for year one, legal templates from Cooley, tax guidance from PwC
6. Atlas e-signs and files everything; **incorporation completes in ~1-3 business days**
7. Once incorporated, log in to your Stripe Dashboard → **Atlas → Perks** to claim partner offers individually

**Important:**
- After year 1, **registered agent renewal is $100/year**
- Founders from **140+ countries** are supported (no US residency needed)
- You'll need a **US EIN before you can open a Mercury / Brex bank account** — Atlas gets you the EIN in ~1-2 weeks
- The $500 is non-refundable once incorporation is filed

## Partner Perks (the $50,000+ headline)

All perks are accessible from the **Atlas → Perks** section of the Stripe Dashboard after incorporation. Amounts and terms are set by each partner and change periodically — verify current offers in the dashboard before counting on a specific number.

### AI / ML Credits (most relevant for AI builders)

**Reality check:** Stripe advertises "$50K+" as the cumulative ceiling. In practice, founders typically claim **$5K-$15K of usable value** depending on their tool stack. Don't pick Atlas just for the perks — pick it because you actually need a Delaware C-Corp.

---

## Eligibility

- **Anyone in 140+ countries** can incorporate via Atlas (you don't need to be a US resident or citizen)
- You must be the **company founder** and able to legally form a US company
- **Restricted business categories** (gambling, adult, regulated finance, etc.) are not supported — see [Atlas restricted categories](https://support.stripe.com/questions/stripe-atlas-restricted-business-categories)
- For the **HubSpot 90% tier** specifically: you must also be backed by an approved VC, accelerator, or incubator
- For **AWS Activate $5K**, **Google Cloud larger tiers**, etc., partners do their own approval — being an Atlas member gets you the application slot, not an automatic grant

---

## Who This Is (and Isn't) For

**Good fit:**
- Solo founder or small team that needs a real **US C-Corp** for fundraising or US customers
- Non-US founder who wants to invoice US clients in USD via Stripe
- AI startup that wants the OpenAI + Anthropic + AWS credit stack without cobbling together separate applications
- Anyone who would otherwise pay a lawyer $1,500-$3,000 to incorporate

**Bad fit:**
- You only want the AI credits — apply directly to [OpenAI Startups](https://openai.com/forms/startup-program/) and [Anthropic Startups](https://www.anthropic.com/startups) instead, no $500 incorporation needed
- You're a non-US founder running a local business — a US C-Corp creates real ongoing tax obligations (Form 5472, Delaware franchise tax, ~$450/yr minimum even with zero revenue)
- You already have a US LLC/Corp — Atlas doesn't help you migrate; you're outside the perk ecosystem

---

## Ongoing Obligations (the Catch)

- **Delaware franchise tax**: ~$450/year minimum (C-Corp), due March 1
- **Form 5472 + Form 1120**: required annually if you have a foreign owner — penalty for missing is $25,000
- **Federal tax return**: required even if zero revenue
- **Registered agent**: $100/year after year 1 (Atlas auto-renews unless cancelled)
- **State income tax**: depends on where you operate from

Atlas provides the templates and PwC guidance, but **filing is on you**. Most founders use Atlas-recommended firms (e.g., Pilot, Mercury Treasury) or DIY.

---

## Additional Tips

- **Claim AI/cloud perks immediately** after incorporation — some have time limits from EIN issuance
- **OpenAI and Anthropic perks** require a separate application through their startup programs; the Atlas dashboard gives you the referral link, not auto-approval
- **AWS Activate** $5K credits are valid for 2 years from issuance — don't claim until you're ready to use them
- **Stripe processing credits** ($2,500) apply automatically to your first ~$2,500 of Stripe fees; effectively waives ~$85K of processing volume at 2.9% + $0.30
- **Mercury 20% off Atlas** — if you're a Mercury customer first, you can get $400 off the $500 fee; check [mercury.com/perks/stripe-atlas](https://mercury.com/perks/stripe-atlas)
- **Don't issue founder stock yourself** — let Atlas handle 83(b) filing; missing the 30-day window is a classic, expensive mistake

At **1 credit = $0.01**, that is $0.25 of credit — enough for ~3 images on the flagship Ultra model (8 credits each), ~8 images on Core (3 credits each), or one Stable Audio 2.5 generation (20 credits). ## Registration (Step-by-Step)

1. Go to [platform.stability.ai](https://platform.stability.ai/).

**Important:**

- If a generation **fails** for content-policy reasons, **credits are still deducted** — budget accordingly when prototyping NSFW-adjacent prompts.

## Submission 184: Singapore Enterprise Compute Initiative - up to SGD 350K cloud credits

- Category: Startup Programs
- Source Link: https://www.disg.gov.sg/enterprise-compute-initiative
- Amount: Up to S$105K consulting support + S$200K–S$350K cloud credits (stretch up to S$1.9M with Oracle private cloud or S$700K Azure agentic AI track)
- Difficulty: 4/5 (Hard)
- Expires At: N/A

### Description

The **Enterprise Compute Initiative (ECI)** is a **S$150 million** government-backed programme run by **Digital Industry Singapore (DISG)** — a joint office of EDB, Enterprise Singapore, and IMDA — announced at Singapore's FY2025 Budget. It pairs Singapore-registered enterprises with one of four major Cloud Service Providers (**AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle**) and a partner consultancy to build a production-grade AI MVP. Each successful applicant gets **up to S$105,000 of consulting support** (70% of up to S$150K costs, you cover the remaining 30%) **plus S$200K–S$350K in cloud credits** (with complementary programmes pushing the cloud-side value as high as **S$1.9M** in some cases).

> **Reality check:** This is **not** a self-serve credit grab. You need a real Singapore-incorporated company with **≥10 local employees**, a tech team, CEO sign-off, and a concrete AI use case. If you're a solo founder or a foreign startup, this is not for you — look at AWS Activate, Google for Startups, or Microsoft for Startups Founders Hub instead.

---

## Who Qualifies (Strict Eligibility)

You must meet **all** of the following baseline criteria:

- **Registered and physically present in Singapore** (UEN required, Corppass needed to apply)
- **CEO-level sponsorship** of the project
- **Minimum 10 Singapore-based employees**
- **Tech team of at least 2** (software engineers, AI engineers, or data scientists)
- **Prior experience building custom AI solutions** (not your first AI project)
- **Access to the relevant datasets** for the proposed use case
- **Financial capability** to complete the project (you fund 30% of consulting + any spend beyond credits)

Your AI use case must demonstrate impact via one of: process improvement, new product development, R&D, or ecosystem contribution. Complex, scalable solutions are prioritised.

---

## Registration (Step-by-Step)

1. **Read the factsheet** — [ECI Factsheet (PDF, updated Oct 2025)](https://www.disg.gov.sg/files/Enterprise_Compute_Initiative_Factsheet_Updated_27_Oct_2025.pdf)
2. **Pick a CSP track** based on your existing stack and use case (AWS / Azure / GCP / Oracle — see breakdown below)
3. **Identify a partner consultancy / system integrator** from the CSP's approved list (Accenture, Deloitte, NCS, PwC, EY, TCS, Avanade, Searce, etc.)
4. **Scope the project** with the consultancy — they help you draft the use-case narrative, datasets, KPIs, and budget (capped at S$150K consulting cost)
5. **Log in to FormSG with Corppass** at the [official application form](https://form.gov.sg/67ef9a05e8b901fcefbe1433)
6. **Submit** the use-case impact assessment, organisational readiness, and infrastructure capability sections
7. **Wait for evaluation** by DISG — selection prioritises impact, scalability, and readiness
8. On approval, you sign with the CSP + consultancy and have **up to 1 year** (often 6 months) to deliver the MVP

**Caveats:**
- Cohorts are **staggered** — each CSP launched its track on a different date and runs for one year from that launch
- You **pay 30%** of consulting costs out of pocket (max S$45K of your money)
- Cloud credits are paid directly to the CSP — you don't see cash
- Questions: email **hello@grants.sg** or use the DISG contact form

---

## Cloud Credits by CSP

| CSP | Programme | Base Credits | Stretch / Complementary | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **AWS** | AI Springboard | **up to S$350,000** | up to **S$600K** via Migration Acceleration Program (MAP) + AWS Lift | Highest baseline credit amount |
| **Microsoft Azure** | Agentic AI Accelerator | **up to S$250,000** | up to **S$700K** for select businesses on agentic AI roadmap co-development | Includes Copilot / Copilot Studio access |
| **Google Cloud** | AI CTO | **up to S$200,000** in training licences + financial incentives | — | Includes 2-week interactive AI/GenAI workshops + certification |
| **Oracle** | ECI Programme | **up to S$250,000** Oracle Cloud Universal Credits | **up to S$1.9M** for enterprises needing private cloud infrastructure | Highest stretch ceiling — best for regulated/large workloads |

---

## Available AI Models & Services

The ECI is **CSP-agnostic** — you get whatever models the chosen provider exposes:

- **AWS:** Amazon Bedrock (Claude, Llama, Mistral, Titan, Nova), SageMaker, Q Developer
- **Azure:** Azure OpenAI (GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-5 family, o-series), Azure AI Foundry, Copilot Studio
- **Google Cloud:** Vertex AI (Gemini 2.x family, Imagen, Veo), Agent Builder, Model Garden
- **Oracle:** OCI Generative AI (Cohere, Llama, Meta), OCI Data Science, AI Quick Actions

Check each CSP's current model catalogue before committing — this list moves monthly.

---

## Partner Consultancies (System Integrators)

You must engage one of the CSP-approved consultancies. Headline partners across the four tracks:

- **Tier 1 / Big 4:** Accenture, Deloitte, PwC Consulting, Ernst & Young Advisory
- **Singapore-anchored:** NCS, Avanade Asia, AvePoint
- **AI / cloud specialists:** Searce, Tatvic Analytics, Axrail, Cloud Kinetics, Boon Software Consulting, TCS

Each CSP has 10–20 approved partners — see the [Cloud Service Providers page](https://www.disg.gov.sg/cloud-service-providers/) for the full list.

---

## Timeline & Cohorts

- **Programme funding announced:** Budget 2025 (Feb 2025)
- **CSP tracks launched:** Staggered through 2025 — Oracle's track was advanced in Jan 2026
- **Each cohort runs:** 1 year from CSP launch date (fast movers finish in ~6 months)
- **Total programme window:** Through 2026+ until the S$150M envelope is exhausted
- **Status:** **Active and accepting applications** as of May 2026

---

## What's the Catch?

- **You co-fund** — 30% of consulting costs (up to S$45K) come out of your pocket
- **No cash** — cloud credits go to the CSP, consulting subsidy goes to the consultancy
- **Singapore-only** — foreign-incorporated entities cannot apply; you cannot "set up an SG entity to qualify" without genuine local headcount
- **Headcount gate** — the **≥10 SG employees** rule eliminates almost all early-stage startups
- **Prior AI experience required** — you can't use ECI to learn AI from zero; you need to show past custom AI work
- **Selective** — not every application is funded; impact and scalability win
- **MVP focus** — the deliverable is a production-grade MVP, not pure R&D exploration

---

## Additional Tips

- **Pick the CSP that matches your stack.** Migrating frameworks mid-project burns credits and time.
- **Engage the consultancy early.** They help shape a winning application and know what DISG approves.
- **AWS** has the highest baseline credit (S$350K) — best if you have no preference.
- **Oracle** has the highest stretch ceiling (S$1.9M) — best for regulated workloads or private cloud needs.
- **Azure** is the strongest pick if your use case centres on **agentic AI** or Copilot extensions.
- **Google Cloud** is the leanest base offer but bundles deep training and certification — great for upskilling teams.
- **Plan for 30% co-funding** in your project budget upfront.
- **DISG is part of EDB / IMDA / Enterprise Singapore** — a successful ECI engagement can open doors to other SG grants (PSG, EDG).

- Expires At: N/A

### Description

**Shadeform** is a **GPU cloud marketplace** ("Kayak for GPUs") that exposes **30+ underlying GPU providers** (Lambda Labs, Nebius, Crusoe, RunPod, CoreWeave, Vultr, DigitalOcean, Vast.AI, TensorDock, plus limited GCP/Azure access) behind **a single unified API and dashboard**. The Free API tier lets you explore the marketplace, list providers, query availability/pricing, and launch up to 1 small GPU instance for short evaluations.

**Critical: This is NOT free GPU compute.** Shadeform itself does not give away GPU hours. The "free" part is the **API access tier** — you can call the marketplace API at no charge. Any GPU instance you actually launch is **billed at the underlying provider's hourly rate plus a 6-12% Shadeform markup**, deducted from your prepaid wallet. If you want truly free GPU credits, look at the providers Shadeform aggregates (e.g. RunPod $1K startup credits, Lambda research grants) directly.

---

## Who This Is For

This offer is useful for you if:

- You want to **evaluate the Shadeform API** before committing — write code, query GPU availability across providers, test the SDK, prototype multi-cloud orchestration.
- You need **occasional, short-lived GPU bursts** across many providers and don't want 30 separate billing relationships.
- You're building tooling on top of GPU marketplaces (e.g. SkyPilot integration, custom orchestration, training pipelines with failover).

It is **not** for you if:

- You expected free GPU hours. There are none here. Use Lightning AI free tier, Google Colab, Kaggle, or apply to provider-specific grants instead.
- You need long-running training jobs (5-day max instance duration on free tier).
- You want the absolute lowest GPU price — direct provider procurement avoids the 6-12% Shadeform markup.

---

## What the Free API Tier Actually Includes

| Limit | Free Tier | Paid Tier |
|---|---|---|
| **API requests per day** | 10 / day | Unlimited |
| **Concurrent GPU instances** | 1 max | Up to 100 |
| **Max instance duration** | 5 days | No limit |
| **GPU compute cost** | Pay-as-you-go (provider rate + 6-12% markup) | Pay-as-you-go (same markup) |
| **Wallet top-up required to launch** | Yes | Yes |

Rate limits are **per API key**, not per account.

---

## Registration (Step-by-Step)

1. Go to [shadeform.com](https://www.shadeform.com/) and click **Sign Up**.
2. Create an account with email + password (or OAuth, depending on what's offered).
3. Verify email if prompted.
4. **Generate an API key** in dashboard **Settings → API Keys**. You can do this for free and start calling read-only API endpoints (list providers, list GPU types, check availability, get pricing) immediately within the 10 req/day cap.
5. **To actually launch a GPU instance**, you must **top up your wallet** with a credit card (any amount; charges are deducted per minute as instances run).
6. Use the API or dashboard to launch an instance — Shadeform automatically routes to the cheapest/most available provider matching your spec, or you can pin to a specific provider.
7. **Terminate the instance manually** when you're done — billing continues by the minute until you stop it.

**Important caveats:**

- **No free GPU hours.** Wallet funds you add are spent on real provider billing.
- **5-day cap** on the free tier means you cannot run a long fine-tune.
- The **10 req/day API cap** burns fast — listing instance types, checking availability, launching, polling status, terminating can easily eat 5-8 calls per single deploy cycle. Plan calls carefully or upgrade.
- **1-minute billing increments** (better than most providers' 1-hour minimums).

---

## What You Pay For GPU Usage

Billing = **underlying provider's hourly rate × time used + Shadeform markup (6-12%)**, billed by the minute.

Approximate examples (rates fluctuate; check the live marketplace):

| GPU | Direct Provider | Approx. via Shadeform |
|---|---|---|
| RTX 3090 | ~$0.22/hr | ~$0.24-$0.25/hr |
| L4 | ~$0.40/hr | ~$0.44-$0.45/hr |
| H100 (80GB) | ~$1.90-$2.50/hr | ~$2.00-$2.70/hr |
| H200 | ~$3.00-$3.50/hr | ~5-8% markup |
| B200 | premium | ~5-8% markup |

Markup is **higher percentage on cheap GPUs**, lower percentage on premium hardware. Shadeform is competitive on convenience, not on raw price — for committed bulk usage (>1,000 hours), direct provider contracts are cheaper.

- **Lambda Labs** (H100, A100)

- **RunPod** (full range, including consumer GPUs)
- **CoreWeave** (enterprise H100 / H200)
- **Vultr**
- **DigitalOcean**
- **Vast.AI** (cheapest spot consumer GPUs)
- **TensorDock**
- Limited **GCP** and **Azure** access

Plus 20+ smaller niche/regional providers spanning **100+ regions** across North America, Europe, Asia, and Australia.

---

## Notable Features (All Tiers)

- **Automatic provider selection** by availability, latency, reliability, cost.
- **Failover** — if one provider goes down or runs out of capacity, Shadeform can transparently switch.
- **Granular 1-minute billing** (most underlying providers require 1-hour minimums; Shadeform passes through finer granularity where supported).
- **Reserved GPU clusters** — multi-GPU clusters up to 64 GPUs available, plus reserved commitments with bulk discounts (paid tier).
- **SkyPilot integration** — Shadeform is now a native cloud in SkyPilot, so you can use the SkyPilot CLI to launch jobs across all aggregated providers via Shadeform.

If the goal is free GPU hours (not API evaluation), look at:

## Am I Eligible?

You must meet **all three** criteria:

**Special cases — apply elsewhere instead:**

5. If approved, the credits are applied to your existing Sentry organization — keep using it as normal, no migration needed

## What's the Catch?

- **No catch on the free tier** — you genuinely don't need a card. Credits don't expire.
- The **Starter plan caps you at 60 RPM**, which is fine for prototyping but you'll feel it on production loads. Going higher RPM requires upgrading (you can't just buy more credits).
- Documentation is bilingual but improving — some pages (e.g. registration flow) are sparse. Use the dashboard UX rather than the docs for the signup walkthrough.
- **Geographic focus:** the platform is engineered for **Indic languages**. Don't expect it to be competitive on European or Mandarin TTS — that's not the product.
- The **₹1,000 vs ₹100 documentation conflict** (see top of page) means you should verify what actually shows up in your dashboard after signup, and screenshot it for your records.

- For voice-first agentic apps in Indian languages, the **Bulbul TTS + Saaras STT + Sarvam-M LLM** combo is the easiest end-to-end Indic stack

- **Effective discount:** ~33% off list (you pay 50K for 75K of usage)

## Submission 177: Recraft: 30 free image/vector credits per day

- Category: AI API Free Tiers

### Description

Recraft's **Free plan** gives every account **30 credits per day**, refreshed every 24 hours. Credits can be spent on raster image generation, vector generation, mockups, AI edits (modify region, erase, recolor, upscale, vectorize, background removal). The same credit balance powers both the **Recraft Studio** (web UI) and the **Recraft API**, so the daily 30 credits are usable programmatically — no paid plan required to call the API. Referrals add **+200 credits per friend**, capped at **4,000 credits** (20 referrals).

**The big catch:** Free-plan output is **owned by Recraft, public** (visible in the community gallery), and carries **no commercial license**. If you need to use generated assets in a product or for a client, you must upgrade to a paid plan — Free is for evaluation, learning, and personal exploration only.

---

## Registration (Step-by-Step)

1. Go to [recraft.ai](https://www.recraft.ai/) and click **"Try for free"** (or **"Sign up"** in the top-right).
2. Sign up with **Google**, **Apple**, or **email + password**. **No credit card required.**
3. You land in Recraft Studio with **30 credits already loaded**. The counter resets every 24 hours from your first generation.
4. To use the API: open **Profile menu → API → Generate Token** (the API page is reachable from the user menu). Copy the bearer token.
5. Test it (OpenAI-compatible-style HTTP):
   ```bash
   curl https://external.api.recraft.ai/v1/images/generations \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_TOKEN>" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"prompt":"a red panda on a skateboard","style":"digital_illustration"}'
   ```

**Important:**
- Free-plan API calls draw from the **same 30/day pool** as the web UI — spend wisely.
- Free plan caps **image uploads at 3 per day** and generates **up to 2 images per prompt**.
- **No credit top-ups on Free** — once 30 credits are gone, you wait 24 h or upgrade.
- Outputs are **public** in the community gallery and **not licensed for commercial use**.

At 1 credit per raster image, 30/day ≈ **~900 raster images/month** for free.

## Submission 176: Prime Intellect Fast Compute Grants ($500-$100K)

- Category: Free GPU & Compute

- Difficulty: 4/5 (Hard)

### Description

**Prime Intellect** runs **Fast Compute Grants** — a rolling, low-bureaucracy grant program awarding **$500-$100,000 in compute credits** on its GPU platform to researchers and builders working on open-source / decentralized AI. The program was launched in 2024 to back "ambitious open-source AI research into novel models, architectures, techniques, and paradigms needed to make open and decentralized AGI a reality." Decisions are returned in **5-10 days** and applications are made by emailing a pitch to **contact@primeintellect.ai**. There are no formal eligibility hoops (no VC backing, no .edu requirement, no nationality restriction) — but the technical bar is explicitly described as high.

Credits are spent on Prime Intellect Compute, an aggregator that brokers GPUs from **50+ underlying providers** (effectively a meta-cloud). The platform exposes both **on-demand instances** (single GPUs up to 256-GPU clusters) and **reserved clusters**, with hourly billing and the option to resell idle reserved capacity back to the spot market.

---

## Is this for me?

**Good fit:**
- Independent researchers, PhD students, postdocs working on open-source AI
- Small teams doing distributed / decentralized training research (federated learning, swarm training, model merging, etc.)
- Builders shipping open-weight models, novel architectures, RL post-training experiments, evals or environments
- Hackers who already have a concrete experiment plan and just need GPUs (not "I want to learn ML")

**Bad fit:**
- Closed-source / proprietary product work — the program is explicitly oriented toward open AI
- People without a clear technical proposal — "the bar for quality is high"
- Anyone needing inference for a SaaS product (use the standard paid platform or one of the cheap free tiers like Groq / Cerebras / Z.AI)

---

## Registration (Step-by-Step)

3. **Wait 5-10 days** for a decision. Approved grants come with credits provisioned to a Prime Intellect account.
4. **Create an account** at [app.primeintellect.ai](https://app.primeintellect.ai/) (Google or email signup) — you can do this before applying so the credits attach to an existing workspace.
5. **Spend the credits** via the dashboard: launch on-demand pods, reserve clusters, or use the platform's RL / training stack.

**Important:**
- This is **email-based** intake — there is no public web form. Do not wait for a fancy application portal.
- "Anyone from anywhere can apply" — no US/EU residency requirement, no need to be at a university or company.
- The credit amount you get is sized to the proposal; don't ask for $100K to fine-tune a 7B on a small dataset.

## What You Get with the Credits

Credits are spent on **Prime Intellect Compute**, which brokers GPUs across 50+ providers. As of May 2026 the on-demand catalog includes:

| GPU | VRAM | Approx. on-demand price |
|---|---|---|
| **NVIDIA B300** | 288 GB | ~$4.99 / hr |
| **NVIDIA B200** | 192 GB | ~$3.49 / hr |

| **NVIDIA GH200, A100, A40** and other professional/legacy SKUs | varies | varies |

Cluster sizes scale from **1 GPU up to 256-GPU on-demand clusters**; larger reserved clusters are quoted within 24h. Pricing varies because the underlying providers compete on price — you can pick the cheapest provider for a given SKU at booking time.

## Target Use Cases (what tends to get funded)

Prime Intellect is the company behind several open distributed-training projects (INTELLECT-1, OpenDiloco, decentralized RL post-training). Proposals that align with their thesis tend to be received better:

- **Distributed / decentralized training** — federated learning, low-communication optimizers, swarm training, model merging
- **Open-weight model training and fine-tuning** — especially novel architectures or training recipes
- **RL post-training and agent research** — reasoning models, tool-use agents, multi-turn environments
- **Open evals, environments, and benchmarks** — anything that becomes a public artifact
- **Inference research** — speculative decoding, quantization, serving optimizations on open models

Closed-source product work, generic API consumption, and "learning projects" are less likely to be funded.

## Selection Criteria & Catch

- **Bar is quality, not paperwork.** Selection is discretionary and based on the technical merit of the proposal and the credibility of the applicant. There is no published acceptance rate.
- **Open-by-default expectation.** While not always a hard requirement, grantees are encouraged (and frequently expected) to publish their work — code, models, write-ups — so the broader open-AI community benefits.
- **Promotion in exchange for visibility.** Selected projects are amplified through Prime Intellect's channels and partner network.
- **Credits are platform-locked.** They can only be spent on Prime Intellect Compute — not transferred to other providers or cashed out.
- **No published expiry**, but treat the credits as use-it-or-lose-it within a few months; clarify the window when accepting.

## Related Offers from Prime Intellect

- **$100 free credits for Akash GPU integration users** — separate small promo for users trying the Akash decentralized GPU pool through Prime Intellect.
- **Reserved-cluster spot resale** — once you hold a reserved cluster you can resell idle hours back to the spot market, effectively reducing your net burn.
- **ICLR / conference promos** — Prime Intellect periodically announces conference-tied free-compute pushes (ICLR 2024, NeurIPS, etc.). Worth checking their X/Twitter (@PrimeIntellect) before relevant deadlines.

---

## Additional Tips

- **Apply with a concrete experiment, not an idea.** "I want to train an MoE" is weaker than "I want to reproduce X paper at Y scale on Z dataset, expected cost ~600 H100-hours, here is the training script."
- **Show prior work.** A GitHub repo or short technical blog post dramatically improves your odds — it removes the reviewer's risk that you can't actually use the GPUs.
- **Cite Prime Intellect's own research** if relevant (INTELLECT-1, OpenDiloco, PRIME-RL). Alignment with their roadmap is a tailwind.
- **Don't pad the ask.** Asking for $100K when you really need $5K is a red flag; asking for what you actually need is a positive signal.
- **If rejected, ship something small first** on the cheap on-demand tier (~$0.47/hr H200 spot) and re-apply with results.
- **Cheaper alternatives** for small experiments: free tiers from Groq, Cerebras, SambaNova, Together AI, or the always-free Z.AI GLM-Flash models. Use Fast Compute Grants for *training*, not inference exploration.

## Registration (Step-by-Step)

If you're a **small open-source project earning under $200K/year**, you can request that the **12-month expiry be waived** so credits last longer. Contact PostHog support after acceptance.

## What Happens When Credits Expire

1. Credits run for **12 months** from acceptance, OR until you've burned through the $50K, whichever comes first.
2. When credits hit zero, you're **automatically transitioned to the standard paid plan** — no service interruption, but billing kicks in.
3. PostHog automatically emails you an offer for a **one-time $500 credit bonus** to soften the transition.
4. From that point you pay PostHog's normal **usage-based pricing** (free tier of 1M events / 5K replays / 1M flags is still ongoing — set [billing limits](https://app.posthog.com/organization/billing) to avoid surprises).

**Tip:** $50K is a *lot* of PostHog usage (their list pricing puts that at ~25M+ events/month for a year). Most early-stage startups never burn through it before the 12 months expire.

---

## Difficulty: Why Rank 3

- Need a **real company** with website + funding history (not just an indie hacker side project — though bootstrapped solo founders with a real product do get accepted).
- Need a **payment method on file** before applying.
- Approval is automated but **manually reviewed afterward** — fake/empty applications get revoked.
- No VC/accelerator referral required (which is what would push it to Rank 4), and no competitive selection (which would be Rank 5).

---

## Additional Tips

- **Apply early** — the clock starts at acceptance, not when you start using the product. Don't apply on day one if you're not ready to instrument.
- **Combine with the EU region** if you have GDPR-sensitive customers — credits work across regions.
- **Y Combinator startups**: separate, longer-running deal exists historically — check the YC Bookface dealbook before using the public form.
- **Sister-company gotcha**: applying multiple times from related entities (same founders, different LLCs) is caught at review. Apply once, with the entity that will actually use the data.
- **Compare with**: [Mixpanel for Startups](https://mixpanel.com/startups), [Amplitude Scholarship](https://amplitude.com/startup-scholarship) — PostHog tends to be the most generous credit-wise but check pricing fit for your event volume.

## Submission 174: Pinecone for Startups - free Standard Tier + Pro Support

- Category: Startup Programs
- Source Link: https://www.pinecone.io/startup-program
- Amount: Free Standard Tier (waives $70/mo base) + Pro Support + dedicated Slack + variable usage credits (commonly cited as ~$5K bootstrapped / up to ~$150K funded — not officially published)
- Difficulty: 3/5 (Medium)
- Expires At: N/A

### Description

**Pinecone for Startups** gives qualifying early-stage companies free access to Pinecone's **Standard Tier** (normally $70/month base fee) plus **Pro Support**, deployment in any cloud/region, **RBAC**, **Backups**, **Import**, **Prometheus Metrics**, a **dedicated Slack channel**, and additional **usage credits and discounts**. Pinecone is a managed serverless vector database widely used for RAG, semantic search, and AI memory layers — this program removes the base subscription cost and the support paywall so you can ship a production-grade vector store without infrastructure headaches.

---

## Eligibility

Both criteria must be true:

- **< 100 employees**, AND
- **Series A or earlier** (pre-seed, seed, Series A — bootstrapped is fine; Series B and later are out)

There is no requirement to be backed by a specific VC, accelerator, or YC batch — any startup that meets the size + stage bar can apply. Solo founders and bootstrapped teams qualify.

---

## What's Included

### Standard Tier (free for program members)

The Standard Tier normally costs **$70/month base** (plus usage). Program members get the base fee waived and unlock these features:

| Feature | Benefit |
|---|---|
| **Multi-cloud / multi-region deployment** | Deploy indexes in AWS, GCP, or Azure across all supported regions (Starter is single-region only) |
| **RBAC (Role-Based Access Control)** | Org-level user roles and permissions for team collaboration |
| **Backups** | Point-in-time backups of serverless indexes for recovery |
| **Import** | Bulk import vectors from object storage (S3, GCS) — much cheaper than streaming upserts at scale |
| **Prometheus Metrics** | Scrape index metrics into your own observability stack |
| **Higher project / index limits** | Multiple projects, more indexes per project than Starter |
| **Pay-as-you-go usage** | Beyond credits, you only pay for what you use (storage, reads, writes) |

### Pro Support

- **Dedicated Slack channel** with Pinecone engineers for direct support
- Faster response SLAs than the public community / email support
- Architecture guidance for scaling RAG / vector workloads

### Usage Credits

Pinecone does **not publish a fixed credit amount** on the public landing page. Reported figures from third-party startup-credits aggregators (verify during your application call):

- Bootstrapped / no funding raised: roughly **$5,000 in credits** for ~6 months
- Funded startups: up to **~$150,000 in credits** for up to 2 years (negotiated case-by-case)

Treat these as ballpark — the official source only says "usage credits and discounts." The actual amount is set during the application/sales conversation based on your stage and projected usage.

---

## Registration (Step-by-Step)

1. Go to [pinecone.io/startup-program](https://www.pinecone.io/startup-program/)
2. Click **"Apply now"** (or scroll to the application form). If no form is visible, email **startups@pinecone.io** directly
3. Provide:
   - Company name + website
   - Team size (must be < 100)
   - Funding stage (must be Series A or earlier — include latest round details if applicable)
   - Use case / what you're building with Pinecone
   - Expected usage (helps them size your credit grant)
4. Pinecone reviews and replies — typically within a few business days
5. If approved, you'll be onboarded onto the Standard Tier, added to a **dedicated Slack channel**, and your credits will be applied to your billing account

**Tips:**
- If you already have a Pinecone Starter (free) account, you can apply to upgrade — your existing indexes carry over
- Be specific about your use case and traffic projections; vague applications get smaller credit grants
- A working prototype or live product strengthens the application but is not required

---

## What's the Catch?

- **No fixed published credit amount** — the headline benefit (free Standard Tier) is guaranteed if you qualify, but the dollar credits are negotiated. Set expectations accordingly
- **Approval required** — not instant; there is a human review step (usually a few days)
- **Usage beyond credits is billed** — once you exhaust credits or exceed Standard Tier inclusions, you pay standard pay-as-you-go rates (storage per GB, reads/writes per RU/WU)
- **Stage cap is real** — once you raise a Series B, you graduate out of the program (you keep your account, but the free Standard Tier ends and you transition to standard pricing)
- **No fixed end date published** for the free Standard Tier — most credit-aggregator sources cite **12 months** as the typical term; confirm during onboarding

---

## Alternatives to Consider

- **Pinecone Starter (free, no application)** — single-region, single-project, limited indexes, no Pro Support. Good enough for prototypes; you don't need the startup program until you need multi-region or RBAC
- **Pinecone Standard Trial** — newer accounts can get a time-limited Standard Tier trial without the startup program (see [Standard Trial docs](https://docs.pinecone.io/guides/organizations/manage-billing/standard-trial))
- If you don't qualify (Series B+ or 100+ employees) — there's no free path beyond Starter; you pay the $70/mo base + usage

---

## Additional Tips

- The Slack channel is genuinely useful — Pinecone engineers respond fast, and you can get architecture review for free
- Use **Import** (not streaming upserts) for any backfill > a few million vectors — it's drastically cheaper and is included in Standard Tier
- Backups are not enabled by default — turn them on in the console after onboarding
- Pair the program with **AWS Activate** or **GCP for Startups** to also offset the underlying cloud egress / data transfer costs

## Submission 173: Pawsey Summer Internship - paid HPC/AI internship + Setonix supercomputer allocation

- Category: Education & Student
- Source Link: https://pawsey.org.au/supercomputing/training/summer-internships
- Amount: Paid 12-week stipend (~AUD $8K-$12K, co-funded) + allocation on Setonix (AMD MI250X GPU cluster) + 1-week pre-internship workshop
- Difficulty: 3/5 (Medium)
- Expires At: N/A

### Description

The **Pawsey Summer Internship Program** is a 12-week **paid internship** (late November to mid-February, with a 2-week shutdown over the end-of-year holidays) at the **Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre** in Perth, Western Australia. Interns work on real AI/ML/HPC research projects under a domain expert supervisor, with allocations on **Setonix** — currently Australia's most powerful supercomputer — and a 1-week residential **Pre-Internship Workshop** that teaches Linux, MPI/OpenMP, GPU programming with HIP, and Pawsey's tooling. This is one of the easiest ways for an Australian student to get hands-on time with a top-30 global supercomputer **and** get paid to do it.

---

## Registration (Step-by-Step)

This is a **two-sided program** — Researchers/Supervisors propose projects first, then Students apply to those projects.

### For students (typical cycle)

1. Wait for the **Call for Students** to open. The annual cycle for the upcoming summer typically runs:
   - **Call for Projects** — opens around April–May, closes around mid-June
   - **Call for Students** — opens around July–August, closes around late August / early September
   - **Selection + offers** — September–October
   - **Pre-Internship Workshop** — mid-November
   - **Internship runs** — late November to mid-February
2. Browse the published list of accepted projects on the [Pawsey Summer Internship page](https://pawsey.org.au/supercomputing/training/summer-internships/).
3. Submit your application via the Pawsey portal. You'll need:
   - Academic transcript
   - CV / resume
   - A short statement of interest naming **up to 3 preferred projects**
   - Evidence of your full-time Australian working rights (citizenship, PR, or appropriate visa)
4. Shortlisted candidates may be interviewed by the supervising researcher.
5. If accepted, you'll be matched to a project, sign a Pawsey internship agreement, and onboard for the November bootcamp.

### For supervisors / project owners

- Submit a project via the **Call for Projects** in April–June. Pawsey runs a **co-funding model**: Pawsey contributes part of the stipend, the host project / institution contributes the rest. Projects without co-funding are not selected.

**Important:**
- Today is **2026-05-09** — the **2026/27 cycle Call for Projects is the relevant one to track right now**. Check the page above for exact 2026/27 dates as they're published.
- The internship is **in-person in Perth, WA by default**. Remote/hybrid options have been offered in past cycles for students based at partner institutions outside WA — confirm with your supervisor.
- The project pool is curated by Pawsey's research staff and partners (CSIRO, AAO, ICRAR, Curtin, UWA, Monash, etc.) — you can't propose your own project as a student.

---

## Eligibility (Who qualifies)

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Enrollment** | Enrolled at an **Australian higher education institution** at time of application |
| **Level** | 2nd / 3rd year undergraduate, **Honours**, **Master's by research**, or **PhD** |
| **Work rights** | **Full-time working rights in Australia** for the entire 12-week period (citizen, PR, or visa with unrestricted work rights). International students on standard 482/500 study visas with the 48-hr/fortnight cap are typically **ineligible** unless they're on a research-track visa with full work rights. |
| **Discipline** | Any discipline whose project benefits from HPC / AI / ML / data — astronomy, bioinformatics, climate, fluid dynamics, materials, NLP, computer vision, etc. |
| **Skills** | Some prior Linux + Python (or C/C++/Fortran) experience strongly recommended. The Pre-Internship Workshop fills the rest. |

This program is **not open** to students at non-Australian universities, working professionals, or applicants without AU work rights.

---

## What You Get

- **Paid stipend** for the full 12-week period. Pawsey doesn't publish a single fixed dollar amount because it's co-funded with the host researcher — historical reporting has placed it in the **AUD ~$8K–$12K range** for the 12 weeks (varies by year, project tier, and supervising institution top-up). Confirm the current rate with the project supervisor when you apply.
- **Allocation on Setonix** (CPU + GPU partitions) for the duration of the project.
- **1-week Pre-Internship Workshop** in mid-November — Linux, supercomputing concepts, MPI / OpenMP, HIP / ROCm GPU programming, Slurm, Pawsey filesystems, profiling, visualisation. Travel + accommodation typically covered for non-WA participants.
- **Final symposium** at the end of the cycle — you present your work; selected projects get publication / poster opportunities at conferences such as **eResearch Australasia** or **SC**.
- **Co-author credit** on resulting papers / blog posts where applicable.
- **Pawsey alumni network** — prior interns regularly transition into Pawsey staff roles, PhD positions, or industry HPC/AI roles.

---

## Setonix (Compute Resource You'll Use)

Setonix is an **HPE Cray EX** system in Perth, Australia's most powerful supercomputer (~50 PFLOPs theoretical peak, top-30 globally at launch).

| Component | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Architecture** | HPE Cray EX with **Slingshot-11** 200 Gb/s interconnect |
| **CPU partition** | ~200,000 AMD **EPYC "Milan"** cores across ~1,600 nodes |
| **GPU partition** | **192 GPU nodes**, each with **8 logical AMD Instinct MI250X GPUs** (4 physical MI250X cards × 2 GCDs) and **1× AMD EPYC "Trento"** 64-core CPU |
| **GPU memory** | 128 GB HBM2e per MI250X card (64 GB per logical GPU); ~3.2 TB/s memory bandwidth per card |
| **GPU node RAM** | 256 GB (standard) or 512 GB (38 high-memory nodes) |
| **GPU peak** | ~383 TFLOPs FP16 per MI250X; ~35 PFLOPs total in the GPU partition |
| **Software stack** | **ROCm + HIP** (not CUDA), Cray PE, Slurm, Singularity / Apptainer containers, PyTorch + JAX builds for ROCm, plus standard HPC libs |
| **Storage** | Lustre scratch + project filesystems, plus **Acacia** S3 object store for long-term data |

**Heads-up for AI/ML interns:** the GPU partition is **AMD, not NVIDIA**, so you'll be running **ROCm** rather than CUDA. PyTorch and JAX both have ROCm builds and Pawsey provides containers, but expect to spend some onboarding time porting CUDA-only code. The Pre-Internship Workshop covers HIP and ROCm explicitly.

See [Setonix on Pawsey](https://pawsey.org.au/systems/setonix/) and the [Setonix GPU Partition Quick Start](https://pawsey.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/US/pages/51928618/Setonix+GPU+Partition+Quick+Start).

---

## Tips & Gotchas

- **Apply early to multiple projects.** Some popular projects (LLM-related, astronomy ML) get many more applicants than spots. Listing 2–3 projects in your statement strongly improves your odds.
- **Talk to the supervisor before submitting.** A short "hi, I'm interested in your project, here's why" email to the listed researcher massively improves your chances of being shortlisted — this is normal and encouraged.
- **Visa / work rights issue is a hard gate.** International students on standard study visas with the 48-hr/fortnight cap will not pass eligibility for the full-time 12-week internship.
- **GPU code is AMD/HIP, not NVIDIA/CUDA.** If your project uses PyTorch or JAX you're fine (ROCm builds work), but custom CUDA kernels won't run as-is. Plan time for porting.
- **Stipend is taxable Australian income** — if you're an international student or first-time worker, sort out your TFN early.
- **Co-funding is real.** If the supervising researcher couldn't secure their share of the stipend, the project is dropped. Don't be surprised if a project disappears between Call for Projects and Call for Students.

---

## Related Pawsey Programs (if you don't qualify for the summer internship)

- **Pawsey Expert Help Desk** — free for any Australian researcher with a Pawsey allocation.
- **Pawsey Training** — free workshops (HIP, MPI, Singularity, AI on Setonix) open to anyone, including international participants in many cases.
- **Partner Allocation Scheme** — free Setonix time for researchers at Pawsey partner institutions (Curtin, UWA, Murdoch, ECU, CSIRO, AAO).
- **Merit Allocation Scheme (NCMAS)** — the national peer-reviewed allocation scheme for larger Setonix allocations; open to AU-based researchers.
- **EuroHPC LUMI / NCI Gadi** — if you're a researcher needing more compute, NCI Australia (Gadi) and EuroHPC LUMI are the other major HPC options for AU and EU researchers respectively.

- Difficulty: 3/5 (Medium)
- Expires At: 2026-12-31

### Description

Deutsche Telekom's sovereign European public cloud (rebranded from **Open Telekom Cloud** to **T Cloud Public** in 2026) gives new **business** customers a **€250 starter credit** when they redeem the voucher code at booking. The credit is valid for **2 months from contract conclusion** and the voucher itself must be redeemed by **31 December 2026**. Infrastructure runs in certified high-security datacenters in Germany (Magdeburg, Biere) and the Netherlands (Amsterdam), with a separate Swiss variant — fully GDPR-compliant, ISO 27001 / TISAX / BSI C5 certified, and outside the reach of US CLOUD Act / FISA jurisdiction. Useful for European startups and SMEs that need an EU-sovereign alternative to AWS/Azure/GCP, especially for AI workloads where data residency matters.

## Who This Is For (and Who It Isn't)

**You qualify if:**
- You are a **registered business** (sole trader, GmbH, UG, Ltd., SAS, etc.) based in **Europe**
- You can provide company information (company name, address, VAT ID, contact)

**You do NOT qualify if:**
- You are a **private individual / consumer** — T Cloud Public is explicitly **business-only** ("only offered to business users in Europe")

**Bottom line:** This is not the same kind of frictionless "sign up with email, get $200" trial as AWS or Azure. It is a B2B cloud contract — there is paperwork, you need a real company, and onboarding is meant to be done with their sales hotline rather than a self-service flow.

## Registration (Step-by-Step)

1. Go to [public.t-cloud.com](https://public.t-cloud.com/en) (auto-redirects to `t-cloud-public.com`)
2. Click **"Book directly now"** / **"Get started"** to enter the booking flow
3. **Enter the voucher code at checkout** — the current published code is **`4UTCP250`** (post-rebrand). The legacy code **`4UOTC250`** still appears on older landing pages and may also work; if one is rejected, try the other or call the hotline
4. Provide **company information**: legal name, registered address, VAT ID, contact person, billing email
5. Choose a **billing model**: pay-as-you-go (recommended for a trial) or a Reserved Package (12/24/36 months — only useful if you already know your workload). **Reserved packages do NOT auto-renew.**
6. Configure payment method (SEPA direct debit / invoice — credit card is not the default for B2B accounts here). The eShop allows changing payment methods later
7. Accept the Open Telekom Cloud / T Cloud Public terms
8. Account is provisioned, voucher credit is applied — you have **2 months** of contract time to burn through €250

**Strongly recommended:** call **+800 33044770** (free, 24/7, English-speaking) before booking. The starter-credit flow is meant to go through their sales/onboarding team and they can confirm voucher eligibility for your country and waive friction in your contract.

**Important caveats:**
- After 2 months OR after the €250 is consumed, all running resources **silently transition to pay-as-you-go billing**. There is no auto-shutoff. Set tight budget alerts before deploying anything that costs money
- Cash payouts of unused credit are explicitly excluded
- Credit applies against published list prices only — discounts cannot be combined

## EU Data Residency & Compliance

The single biggest reason to pick this over hyperscalers:

- **Datacenters:** Magdeburg + Biere (Germany, 3 AZs), Amsterdam (Netherlands, 3 AZs); separate Swiss variant with three Swiss-soil AZs
- **Operator:** Deutsche Telekom AG (German company, German law)
- **Compliance:** GDPR, ISO 27001, TISAX, BSI C5
- **Jurisdictional protection:** Outside the reach of the US CLOUD Act / FISA Section 702, unlike AWS/Azure/GCP EU regions
- **AI services:** All AI Foundation Services run on EU infrastructure — your prompts and embeddings don't leave the EU

For EU-regulated industries (healthcare, finance, government, regulated SaaS targeting European enterprises) this is often the difference between "can deploy in production" and "can't".

---

## Additional Tips

- **The €250 will not last long on GPU workloads.** An H100 instance burns through it in under 24 hours of continuous use. Treat the credit as exploration budget, not a free training run
- **Cheaper alternatives if you don't need EU sovereignty:** Hetzner Cloud, Scaleway, OVHcloud all give EU residency at lower price points without the B2B contract overhead
- **For pure AI exploration without infra friction:** the AI Foundation Services API is the most interesting piece — it lets you call Llama 3.3 / Mistral Small 3 / DeepSeek R from EU-hosted endpoints similarly to how you'd use Together or Fireworks, but with sovereign data handling
- **Hotline first, signup second.** Unlike self-service hyperscaler trials, the starter-credit flow really is designed to be onboarded by a human. The hotline is free, 24/7, and English-speaking — use it. They can also confirm whether your country qualifies for the voucher
- **No trade-register filing required upfront**, but you must provide a valid company name + address + VAT ID. Sole traders / freelancers (Einzelunternehmer, auto-entrepreneur) generally qualify

### Description

Notion for Startups gives qualifying early-stage companies **up to 6 months free of the Notion Business plan with Notion AI included**. Three tiers exist depending on how you apply: **6 months** for startups referred by a partner VC/accelerator, **3 months** for non-partner startups building scalable tech products, and **1 month** as a fallback for SMBs or partial applications. ## Registration (Step-by-Step)

If the reviewer can't fully verify you (incomplete site, only personal socials, solo applicant looking like an individual), the team often grants a **1-month** trial of the Business plan with Notion AI instead of rejecting outright.

- **Cannot stack** with other Notion discounts, codes, or promos.
- **No refunds** for invoices you already paid before applying.
- The credit applies to **one workspace** only, not to your whole org if you have multiple workspaces.
- After the free period ends, the workspace **auto-converts to paid Business** at $20/user/month unless you downgrade — set a calendar reminder.

## Submission 170: Northflank Free Developer Sandbox (2 Services + Database)

- Category: Cloud Providers
- Source Link: https://northflank.com/pricing
- Amount: 2 services + 2 cron jobs + 1 database + 1 BYOC cluster, always-on, ~10 GB egress, ~1M HTTP req/month, 10 GB logs, 10 GB metrics
- Difficulty: 2/5 (Easy)
- Expires At: N/A

### Description

Northflank's **Developer Sandbox** is a permanently free plan aimed at hobby projects, prototypes, and trying the platform. You get **2 services**, **2 cron jobs**, **1 database/addon**, and **up to 1 BYOC cluster** — meaning you can either run on Northflank's managed cloud or connect your own AWS / GCP / Azure / Oracle Cloud / CoreWeave / Civo / bare-metal account and Northflank acts purely as the orchestration layer. Services are **always-on (no sleeping)**, deploy from any Git repo or OCI image, get free SSL + custom domains, and include API/CLI access.

---

## Registration (Step-by-Step)

1. Go to [northflank.com/pricing](https://northflank.com/pricing) and click **"Get started for free"** (or sign up directly at app.northflank.com)
2. Sign up with **GitHub, GitLab, Google, or email + password**
3. Verify your email if you used the email/password flow
4. **Credit card is requested during sign-up** as anti-abuse verification — you will not be charged unless you actively upgrade to Pay-As-You-Go. The card stays on file with no recurring billing on the Sandbox tier.
5. Create a project, then add up to 2 services, 2 cron jobs and 1 addon (Postgres / MySQL / MongoDB / Redis / etc.)
6. To use **BYOC**: in project settings, add an integration for AWS / GCP / Azure / Oracle / CoreWeave / Civo / bare-metal and create a cluster — Northflank deploys into your account; you pay your cloud provider directly, Northflank's platform fee on Sandbox stays $0.

**Important:**
- Card is required at signup. Northflank states explicitly: **"you won't be charged unless you upgrade to a paid plan."** This puts the friction at Rank 2, not Rank 1.
- The 2/2/1 quota is **per account**, not per project — you cannot multiply free quotas by spinning up more projects.
- The Sandbox is intended for hobby / pre-production usage. Production workloads belong on Pay-As-You-Go.
- BYOC on the Sandbox plan is real: orchestration is free, but **your cloud provider still bills you** for the underlying VMs / disks / egress.

---

## What You Get on Sandbox

| Resource | Free Limit |
|---|---|
| **Services** | 2 (long-running deployments, e.g. web app, API, worker) |
| **Cron jobs** | 2 (scheduled jobs) |
| **Databases / addons** | 1 (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, RabbitMQ, etc.) |
| **BYOC clusters** | Up to 1 (AWS / GCP / Azure / Oracle / CoreWeave / Civo / bare-metal) |
| **Free egress** | ~10 GB included (overages billed at $0.15/GB on PAYG) |
| **HTTP requests** | ~1M/month included |
| **Logs** | 10 GB |
| **Metrics** | 10 GB |
| **Always-on compute** | Yes — no sleep / cold-start hibernation |
| **Free SSL + custom domains** | Yes |
| **API & CLI access** | Yes |
| **GitHub / GitLab / Bitbucket integration** | Yes (auto-deploy on push) |

Compute is described as **"limited"** on Sandbox — Northflank does not publish a specific vCPU / RAM ceiling per service for the free plan. On paid plans the platform scales individual workloads from 0.1 vCPU / 256 MB up to 32 vCPU / 256 GB. Treat Sandbox services as small (think 0.1–1 vCPU, ~512 MB) and run benchmarks before committing real traffic.

---

## BYOC Support

Northflank has one of the broadest BYOC stories in PaaS. On the Sandbox plan you can connect **one** cluster from any of:

- **Public clouds:** AWS, GCP, Azure, Oracle Cloud
- **Alternative GPU/compute clouds:** CoreWeave, Civo
- **On-premises / bare-metal**

The Northflank execution plane runs **inside infrastructure you own**; orchestration, autoscaling and microVM provisioning happen via the Northflank control plane. Any OCI-compliant container image works without modification. This is the angle that makes the Sandbox especially interesting if you already have AWS/GCP credits sitting unused — Northflank becomes the deployment layer at $0 platform cost, you only pay the underlying cloud bill.

---

## What Runs on It

Anything you can package as an OCI/Docker image — Northflank pulls from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or any OCI-compatible registry. Common usage:

- Node.js / Python / Go / Rust / Ruby web apps and APIs
- Background workers and queue consumers
- Cron jobs (data syncs, scheduled scrapers, embedding refreshes)
- A single managed database (Postgres / MySQL / MongoDB / Redis)
- Self-hosted **AI inference services**: deploy a vLLM / Ollama / Hugging Face TGI image as a service and call it from your app (caveat: free-tier compute is small; for serious model serving use BYOC with GPU nodes from CoreWeave/AWS/GCP)

---

## Sandbox vs Paid (Pay-As-You-Go)

| | Developer Sandbox (free) | Pay-As-You-Go |
|---|---|---|
| **Services** | 2 | Unlimited |
| **Cron jobs** | 2 | Unlimited |
| **Databases** | 1 | Unlimited |
| **BYOC clusters** | 1 | Unlimited |
| **Compute size** | Limited | 0.1–32 vCPU, 256 MB – 256 GB |
| **Card on file** | Yes (not charged) | Yes (charged on usage) |
| **Production-ready** | No (hobby / prototyping) | Yes |

Upgrading is a flag flip — you stay on the same projects, just remove the quota cap.

---

## Student Upgrade (Free, Bigger Sandbox)

If you have a student email, Northflank runs a separate **Student Developer Pack** that bumps the free tier to:

- **4 services** (vs 2 on default Sandbox)
- Student-tier support

To claim: email **students@northflank.com** from your student email address ([northflank.com/student-developer-pack](https://northflank.com/student-developer-pack)). They follow up with the upgrade. No SheerID / form — purely email-based verification.

---

## Additional Tips

- **No automatic upgrade to paid.** You won't "silently" get billed when you hit the 2/2/1 limit — Northflank just refuses to create the 3rd service until you switch to PAYG.
- **Use the BYOC angle** if you've burned through Northflank's small Sandbox compute but still want free orchestration: connect an AWS account that already has AWS Activate credits, and Northflank's $0 platform fee stacks with your AWS credit.
- **Egress is the trap on PAYG.** $0.15/GB adds up fast for video/file delivery. On Sandbox you have 10 GB/month free; design around that if you're serving traffic from Northflank-managed compute (BYOC egress is billed by your cloud, not by Northflank).
- **Permanent free.** Unlike $200/30-day-style trials, the Sandbox plan is ongoing and renews indefinitely as long as you stay within the 2/2/1 quota.
- **Region locking is per-cluster on BYOC.** When you bring your own cloud, you pick the region; Northflank-managed regions are listed in-app at cluster creation time.

## Submission 169: Neon Startup Program - up to $100K in serverless Postgres credits

- Category: Startup Programs
- Source Link: https://neon.com/startups
- Amount: Up to $100,000 in Neon credits (actual grant varies by stage and projected scale)
- Difficulty: 4/5 (Hard)
- Expires At: N/A

### Description

Up to **$100,000 in Neon credits over 12 months** for serverless Postgres workloads — production databases, dev/preview environments, branching, read replicas, autoscaling, and scale-to-zero. Bundled with **engineer support during onboarding**, **early access to new features**, **priority support**, and co-marketing opportunities (launch stories, joint technical content). Reviewed on a rolling basis, no warm intro required, but you do need verifiable VC funding.

---

## Is This For You?

**You qualify if:**
- You're a **VC-backed startup** that has raised between **$1M and $5M** in institutional funding (any institutional investor — they don't have to be one of Neon's partner VCs)
- You **launched a product within the past 12 months** (early-stage / MVP / recently GA)
- You're building software that needs a fast, scalable, modern Postgres database
- You can verify your funding (cap table screenshot, term sheet, Crunchbase entry, or investor reference)

**You do NOT qualify if:**
- You're bootstrapped / pre-funding / friends-and-family only — institutional VC is required
- You've raised significantly more than $5M (you're past the early-stage window this program targets — actual credit grant scales down with stage)
- Your product launched more than ~12 months ago
- You're an agency, consultancy, or services business (the program is for product startups)

**Note on the $100K headline:** the maximum award is $100K but actual grants "vary based on stage, use case, and projected scale." Earlier-stage startups with smaller projected workloads typically receive less. Treat $100K as a ceiling, not a default.

---

## Registration (Step-by-Step)

1. Go to [neon.com/startups](https://neon.com/startups)
2. Click **"Apply now"** (or scroll to the application form on the page)
3. Fill in the short application form. Expected fields:
   - Founder name + work email (use your company domain, not Gmail/personal)
   - Company name + website (must be live)
   - Total funding raised + lead investor(s)
   - Current stage (pre-seed / seed / Series A)
   - When you launched your product
   - Brief description of your use case for Postgres / Neon
   - Estimated monthly Neon spend or scale projection
4. Submit. Neon **reviews applications on a rolling basis** and typically responds **within a few business days** (no fixed deadlines).
5. If approved, Neon applies the credit grant to your existing Neon org (create a Neon account at [console.neon.tech](https://console.neon.tech) first if you haven't) and connects you with an onboarding engineer.

**Important:**
- **No warm introduction is required** — apply cold, even if your VC isn't a Neon partner
- Have your funding evidence ready (term sheet, Crunchbase listing, investor confirmation email) — verification is the main gate
- Sign up for a free Neon account *before* applying so the credits can be applied to an existing org
- Credits are valid for **12 months from approval** — plan your migration / production cutover so you actually use them within that window

---

## What You Can Spend Credits On

Credits apply to all Neon serverless Postgres usage, including:

| Feature | What It Does |
|---|---|
| **Serverless Postgres** | Fully managed Postgres 15/16/17 with separation of compute and storage |
| **Autoscaling** | CPU, memory, connections scale automatically — no manual resizes |
| **Scale to zero** | Pay nothing for compute when the database is idle |
| **Database branching** | Spin up production-like preview/staging branches in seconds (great for PR previews and testing migrations) |
| **Read replicas** | Add read replicas without provisioning new infra |
| **Connection pooling** | Built-in PgBouncer — handle thousands of serverless connections |
| **Instant restore / PITR** | Point-in-time recovery from history |
| **Built-in Auth** | Neon Auth (managed user auth integrated with Postgres) |
| **Data API (REST)** | Auto-generated REST endpoints over your tables |

Useful for: Next.js / Vercel apps, Cloudflare Workers, Supabase migrations, agent memory stores, RAG metadata, multi-tenant SaaS with branch-per-tenant patterns.

This is the main eligibility check. Neon will want to confirm you actually raised $1M+ from institutional investors. Acceptable evidence typically includes:

- A **press release or TechCrunch article** announcing the raise
- A **redacted term sheet** or **SAFE** from a recognized institutional investor
- A **direct intro / reference email** from one of your investors

Friends-and-family rounds, revenue-based financing, debt, and accelerator-only checks (without follow-on institutional capital) generally do NOT meet the $1M institutional bar.

## Additional Tips

- Expires At: N/A

### Description

Nebius (European AI-native cloud, NASDAQ: NBIS) awards **GPU cloud credits and Token Factory inference tokens** to academic researchers. The headline allocation is **up to 8 GPUs for one full year** for training/HPC workloads, plus **up to 10M tokens** for inference via Nebius Token Factory (60+ open-source models, OpenAI-compatible API). Applications open in **monthly two-week windows** with up to 6 winners selected each cycle for the **2026-2027 academic year**.

This is the Nebius **research credits / research grants program** (the two terms are used interchangeably on Nebius' own site). It is a research-track grant — not a startup or hobbyist offer — so eligibility is gated to people affiliated with accredited institutions.

---

## Is This For You?

**Yes, if:**
- You are a **postgraduate (master's), PhD student, postdoc, or faculty member** at an accredited university or non-profit research institution
- You have a concrete AI / ML / data analytics / HPC research proposal that needs GPU compute
- You can describe expected resource usage and outputs (papers, open models, datasets)
- You are OK with Nebius co-marketing the fact that you used their compute

**No, if:**
- You are an undergraduate without a research role
- You are a startup, hobbyist, or independent researcher unaffiliated with an accredited institution → use [Nebius Startups](https://nebius.com/startups/apply) or pay-as-you-go instead
- You have already received a Nebius Research grant (one-shot per person)
- You need credits *now* — review and notification cycles take weeks

---

## What You Get

| Resource | Allocation |
|---|---|
| **GPU compute** | Up to **8 GPUs for 1 year** (training/HPC) |
| **Token Factory inference** | Up to **10,000,000 tokens** across 60+ OSS models |
| **Duration** | 12 months from grant activation |
| **Award size** | "Determined based on the proposal" — 8 GPUs / 10M tokens are the published ceilings |

Nebius does not publicly commit to a specific GPU SKU for grant allocations. Their public GPU lineup includes **HGX H100, H200, B200, B300, GB200 NVL72, and GB300 NVL72** — H100/H200 are the most common Hopper-class workhorses for academic training. Expect Hopper-class hardware unless your proposal specifically justifies Blackwell access.

---

## Registration (Step-by-Step)

1. Go to [nebius.com/nebius-research-credits-program](https://nebius.com/nebius-research-credits-program)
2. Wait for the next **monthly application window** to open (windows are 2 weeks long; check the page for the active window)
3. Click **Apply** and fill in the proposal form. You will be asked for:
   - Your name, institutional email, role (postgrad / PhD / postdoc / faculty), institution
   - Project title and abstract
   - Research objectives, methodology, expected impact
   - **Resource estimate** — how many GPUs, for how long, and roughly how many inference tokens
   - Planned outputs (papers, open-source code, models, datasets)
   - Acknowledgement that Nebius support can be referenced in publications / blog posts
4. Submit before the 2-week window closes
5. Nebius Academy reviews submissions over the next ~3 weeks
6. **Up to 6 winners per cycle** are notified by email
7. On approval, you onboard onto Nebius AI Cloud and Token Factory and credits are activated

**Important caveats:**
- **One application per person, ever** — you cannot reapply if rejected or if your grant ends
- **Only one person per team** can apply for the same project — coordinate with collaborators first
- Awards are **at Nebius' sole discretion** and program terms can change
- Proposals reviewed throughout summer 2026; some applicants notified **late Q3 to early Q4 2026**

---

## Nebius Token Factory — What the 10M Tokens Cover

Token Factory is Nebius' inference platform. The **10M tokens** can be spent across 60+ open-source models, including:

- **Large LLMs:** DeepSeek R1 / V3, Llama-3.3-70B, Qwen2.5-72B, GPT OSS, Mistral-Nemo
- **Reasoning:** QwQ-32B
- **Multimodal:** DeepSeek V3 multimodal
- **Embeddings & safety:** BAAI embeddings, Llama-Guard-3-8B
- **Smaller open models:** Google Gemma-2-27B and others

The API is **OpenAI-compatible** — drop in `https://api.studio.nebius.ai/v1` as the base URL with your Nebius API key and standard `openai` clients work unchanged. For up-to-date model availability and per-token pricing (used to calculate how far 10M tokens stretch), see [Nebius Token Factory](https://nebius.com/services/token-factory).

---

## Region & Data Residency

Nebius is a **European AI-native cloud** with public regions in:

| Region code | Location |
|---|---|
| `eu-north1` | Finland (primary, largest capacity) |
| `eu-west1` | Paris, France |
| `us-central1` | Kansas City, Missouri (US) |
| `me-west1` | Israel |
| `eu-north2` | Iceland (private/select-access) |
| `uk-south1` | UK (opened Q4 2025, private/select-access) |

For academic projects with EU GDPR or data-sovereignty constraints, this is one of the few independent EU-based GPU clouds at scale.

## How This Compares to Other Academic Programs

| Program | Best for | Cadence |
|---|---|---|
| **Nebius Research Credits** (this) | EU/global academics needing 1-yr training GPU access | Monthly, 6 winners/cycle |
| [NAIRR Pilot](https://nairrpilot.org/opportunities/allocations) | US-based researchers | Rolling, 3-week turnaround |
| [EuroHPC AI Factories](https://www.eurohpc-ju.europa.eu/ai-factories/ai-factories-access-modes_en) | EU public-funded research, larger LUMI-class allocations | Calls throughout the year |
| [DOE INCITE Early Career](https://doeleadershipcomputing.org/call-for-proposals/) | Early-career researchers (≤10 yrs post-PhD), exascale | Annual (Apr-Jun call) |
| [Lambda Research Grants](https://lambda.ai/) | Academic AI papers needing on-demand GPUs | Rolling |

If you fit Nebius' eligibility, you can apply to several of these in parallel — they don't conflict.
